Here is a story I have never shared before. 28th August 2021 changed the trajectory of both my life and Bewakoof.

A fire broke out in our manufacturing plant and warehouse and lasted 19 hours. It wiped out all the machinery and inventory, worth ₹50 crores. I was there on the ground, watching it unfold in real time. Luckily, no one was hurt that day. 

One of the hardest parts was the timing. 

After 10 years of building, BEWAKOOF® was at its peak. We were at a ₹250+ crore revenue run-rate, breaking even, and receiving serious investor interest. 

Then overnight, everything changed.

We were left staring at ₹100 crores in loans and vendor obligations, with zero monthly revenue.

You spend a decade hoping to become an overnight success.
I became an overnight failure.

The months that followed were the darkest of my life.
Vendors called relentlessly. Banks warned of bankruptcy. Every day felt like survival.

Mentally, I was falling apart. I had nightmares of the fire. I would wake up in panic. I had brain fog and breakdowns. Over time, it started showing up in my body too - pain, heaviness, and a nervous system that just would not switch off.

It took years to get Bewakoof back on its feet.
And honestly, it took years to get myself back on mine.
Most entrepreneurial journeys swing between highs and lows. Mine, for a while, got ugly.

It takes soul to build a company.
It takes pieces of you to rebuild one.

Last month, one of our Experts was mugged on her way back home after a shift. She was physically assaulted and her phone was taken away. She couldn’t press the SOS button because it required unlocking the phone first.

When we built the first version of our Expert App about 1.5 years ago, we had already added an SOS button. We knew that when thousands of people enter homes every day, things can go wrong. At the time, that felt like the right safety layer.

Since then, Snabbit has changed dramatically and we have grown at an exponential rate. But somewhere along the way, our safety systems had not evolved as fast as the company had. 

That is what led us to build Snabbit Kavach - a platform-embedded safety infrastructure designed to proactively protect our Experts. Because safety cannot be reactive. It cannot depend on someone finding a button in a moment of panic. It has to work quietly in the background, detect risk signals, and step in when needed.

As we scale, we will keep pushing for growth, stronger unit economics, and deeper moats. But one thing cannot be compromised. The trust of the women who power this platform.

Because the more time I spend building Snabbit, the more I realize how tough and how extraordinary their journeys truly are. And the least they deserve is to feel safe at work.

Is Cred Garage building another credit score?


All of us have seen pictures of those fancy cars outside the Cred office recently. The curiosity generation was real and once Cred Garage was out, I had to give it a try.

Here are 2 things that, I feel, can really do wonders for Cred if this takes off 👇🏻

👉🏻 The obvious: Auto insurance
Once you enter your vehicle number, all details are automatically fetched by the app. Cred then knows how old your car is, how many challans are pending against it, and a lot more. This gives them enough data to suggest and sell ‘handpicked’ insurance policies to you.

The business here? Apart from a commission, Cred can also potentially charge insurance companies to get listed on the app and to show up on top!

But here’s what’s more interesting 👇🏻

👉🏻 Auto credit score
Since Cred would have collected so much data about your vehicle in the form of pending challans, repairs, insurance, etc. They would have enough data to form a credit score against your vehicle’s health!

Think of a vehicle as a credit card. A missed payment affects your credit score, right? A challan on the car can potentially affect your auto credit score!

And it’s not just based on superficial data. Cred might get access to meaningful financial data such as your refuelling history, details of your insurance policy, car repair history, service frequency and so much more!

Needless to say, they’ll also know the price of the car you own!

For those who don’t have a credit score or have a low credit score, this can be an excellent alternative. If Cred nails it right, it can potentially build a great business just out of this one model!

My unfortunate read on Indian ambition is that it's just preparation for ambition, and we've lost the ability to tell the difference.

Like the credential was supposed to be the door, right? You get a credential and then you use it. But imo it has become the house and now everyone's just redecorating every few years with NO idea what they actually want their home to look like.

The sequence is: get the degree, get the job, get the credibility, THEN take the risk. Except the credibility threshold keeps moving and by the time you've cleared it you have EMIs and your parents finally stopped worrying and the risk feels a lot more scary than it did at 22.

So you don't do it. You become a mentor instead and point someone younger at the same treadmill. 

What's incredibly telling is what we do with people who just...started without waiting for permission. We don't celebrate them, we absorb them. Guest lectures. Fellowships. Honorary titles. The institution needs to stamp you before it can admit you were right.

Anyway what I'm actually saying is: credentials are a way of not finding out if you're good. Every new credential is another year before the terrifying question of if you're actually good needs a real answer. Completely rational if you're trying to stay undefeated in a game you never quite enter.

We're a country that worships risk-takers and systematically raises risk-avoiders and then acts confused when the builders don't come from the pipeline. Kind of insane, I think.

More companies could take a page from Buffer’s playbook. 

I’ve been watching how Buffer reshapes company branding, not by controlling the narrative, but by amplifying it.

They regularly repost their employees’ LinkedIn content.
Proudly. Publicly. Authentically.

It’s a simple act - but a powerful one.

Their company page becomes a window into the real people behind the brand.
It builds trust externally. And loyalty internally.

And it works.

Content shared by employees gets 8x more engagement than content shared by brand channels. (LinkedIn Business)

Why? Because people trust people more than logos.
And Buffer leans into that.

They empower their team to show up and back them by resharing their wins, ideas, and insights.

This is employee advocacy done right.
✅ It boosts reach.
✅ It builds credibility.
✅ It attracts talent who want to work there.

If you’re leading a brand, consider this:
•⁠ Encourage your team to share what they’re working on
•⁠ Make it easy - offer tips, templates, support
•⁠ Repost their content on your company page
•⁠ Celebrate voices, not just results

When employees feel seen, they show up.
And when they show up, your brand wins.

Shoutout to Buffer for leading by example.
